en: The Hymn of Seeking the Support of Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa’s Hand
O Śrī Śeṣaśaila, whose divine form is a beautiful abode;
O Nārāyaṇa, Acyuta, Hari, whose eyes are as long as lotuses;
O You who protect all the worlds with Your playful side-glances!
O Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa, grant me the support of Your hand. || 1 ||
O Lord whose lotus feet are worshipped by Brahmā and the other gods, O Śaṅkhapāṇi,
whose divine hand is beautifully adorned with the glorious Sudarśana;
O ocean of compassion, O refuge, O embodiment of supreme merit!
O Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa, grant me the support of Your hand. || 2 ||

O Śrī Padmanābha, who is to be known through the Vedānta, the helmsman of the ocean of worldly existence, whose lotus feet are worshipped by Kamalā; O sole purifier of the world, the supreme beyond the supreme, the destroyer of sins!
O Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa, grant me the support of Your hand. || 3 ||
O Lord of Lakṣmī, whose true nature is the goal of the Vedas,
who removes defects such as desire, who bestows awakening,
O crusher of the Daityas and others, O Janārdana, O Vāsudeva!
O Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa, grant me the support of Your hand. || 4 ||
O All-pervading Lord, O Enemy of Mura, swiftly remove the threefold suffering;
protect me with compassion, O Lotus-eyed One;
O Viṣṇu, protect me daily as your own disciple.
O Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa, grant me the support of Your hand. || 5 ||
O Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa, whose forehead is beautified by a crown shimmering with gold and the nine gems and by a tilaka of musk;
whose lotus-face is like the orb of the full moon; O lotus-eyed one, grant me the support of Your hand! 6.

O Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa, whose conch-like neck is adorned with a necklace rich in jewels— the play of whose speech grants boons to those who offer salutations— and whose armlets and gems illuminate the quarters of space, grant me the support of Your hand.
O you whose two arms are marked by divine armlets, whose auspicious self is adorned with beautiful bracelets, O long-armed one,
O giver of desires, whose two hands bear the rings of the lord of serpents!
O Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa, grant me the support of Your hand. || 8 ||
O Lord, O ocean of compassion, please lift me up with mercy as I am submerged in the midst of the world-ocean;
and grant me prosperity, which is the cause for the fullness of Dharma.
O Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa, grant me the support of Your hand. || 9 ||
O Lord with delicate limbs anointed with divine unguents,
whose body is clothed in yellow garments, who possesses the luster of the rising sun,
and who wears a beautiful waistband around Your true navel.
O Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa, grant me the support of Your hand. || 10 ||
With the region of his waist firmly bound by a girdle rich with jewels, and the area of his knees resembling a mirror of rubies,
he captivates the entire world with his two shanks.
O Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa, grant me the support of Your hand. || 11 ||
O Lord, O Infinite One, on the day I behold Your feet— which are adorned by the river that alone purifies the world—
all my sins and the darkness within my heart have reached dissolution.
O Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa, grant me the support of Your hand. || 12 ||
O Compassionate One, fallen as I am from the host of enemies such as desire, I have attained [Thee]; even my entire poverty has vanished,
O Merciful One, who beheld me, so wretched, with a gaze moist with pity.
O Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa, grant me the support of Your hand. || 13 ||
Those men on earth who read this work composed by the illustrious Nṛsiṃha-yati— a bee at the lotus feet of Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa— of Puruṣottama;
They attain the supreme state of Murāri. || 14 ||
Thus ends the *Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa Karāvalamba Stotra*, composed by the venerable Śṛṅgeri Jagadguru, Śrī Nṛsiṃhabhāratī Svāmī.
